Mestia and the Svan Towers

Upper Svaneti's main town at 1,500 m — medieval stone defence towers, two strong museums and the trailhead for every route in the region.

Time needed
4 h
From Tbilisi
470 km · 8:30
Road
Paved
Car needed
Crossover / SUV
Season
May–October
Entry
free

Mestia is the administrative and tourist centre of Upper Svaneti, sitting at roughly 1,500 metres in the upper Enguri gorge. What makes it unusual is that its history is not locked inside a museum: the stone defence towers, most of them dating from the ninth to thirteenth centuries, still stand in ordinary family yards. Svan households built them for two overlapping reasons — protection from raiders, and shelter during avalanches and the long blood-feud disputes that shaped local law.

The old quarters of Lanchvali, Lagami and Lekhtagi are separated by footbridges and narrow lanes, and you can walk the lot in half a day. The Svaneti Museum of History and Ethnography holds processional crosses, icons, chased metalwork and manuscripts that survived precisely because the region was so hard to reach; several pieces were hidden in mountain churches for centuries. The Mikheil Khergiani House-Museum, in the tower house of Georgia's most famous climber, is worth a separate half hour.

What you will actually see:

  • Machubi — the traditional Svan house where family and livestock wintered in one hall
  • Seti Square — the town centre, with cafes, the information point and the guide exchange
  • The Cross viewpoint — a short climb above town with the twin summits of Ushba ahead

Mestia is also a base. Routes to the Chalaadi glacier, the Koruldi lakes, the Hatsvali and Tetnuldi ski areas and Ushguli all start here, and the choice of guesthouses and food is the widest in the region.

Practical advice

Plan at least two nights in Mestia; a single-day visit is mostly driving. Late June to late September is the reliable window. The town works in winter too, but the road occasionally closes after avalanches. Weather changes several times a day, so a rain shell and a warm layer are needed even in August. Park at your guesthouse or on the streets around Seti Square and walk everywhere — the centre is tiny. ATMs and a pharmacy are in the centre, but card payment is not universal, so carry some cash in lari.

How to get there from Tbilisi

Mestia is about 470 km and eight to nine hours from Tbilisi. Take the E60 west through Kutaisi and Samtredia to Zugdidi, then turn north past the Enguri dam at Jvari and into the gorge. The 130 km from Zugdidi to Mestia is fully paved but narrow and endlessly winding — count on three hours for that stretch alone. Doing it in one day is possible, but an overnight stop in Kutaisi or Zugdidi makes the trip far more pleasant. The last dependable fuel stations are in Zugdidi and Jvari. A crossover is more comfortable on the long switchbacks, though a sedan will manage.

Nearby places

Ski area

Hatsvali and Tetnuldi Ski Areas

Mestia's two ski zones — Hatsvali with sheltered forest runs, and Tetnuldi, where the lifts pass 3,000 metres.

Lake

Koruldi Lakes

Small alpine pools at 2,740 m above Mestia, facing Mount Ushba — reachable only by 4x4 or on foot.

Mountain

Chalaadi Glacier

The most accessible glacier near Mestia — a short drive up the valley and a two-hour walk to the ice tongue.
